relations: When the hammer head contacts a surface stone, that stone can fracture and eject fragments outward from the pile.
Removing or displacing a load-bearing stone causes stones resting on it to shift and tumble down the slope.
Repeated impacts transfer energy through the loose stack, loosening adjacent rocks so they scatter across the ground.
The swing must reach the pile edge so the head strikes stones rather than passing through empty air.
caption: A sledgehammer is swung at a pile of rocks, scattering and breaking some of them.
